name: Ermirio Pereira de Moraes
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2014-2022); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Ermirio Pereira de Moraes' late father, Jose Ermirio de Moraes, founded family-owned Grupo Votorantim, one of Brazil's largest conglomerates.
Votorantim operates in more than 20 countries in the aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, agribusiness, and cement industries.
The group dates back to 1918, when Jose Ermirio de Moraes bought a textile factory in Sao Paulo.
The family still controls 100% of the business. Ermirio Pereira's sister, Maria Helena, is also a Votorantim shareholder and a billionaire.
Media-shy Ermirio Pereira earned his B.S. in Petroleum Engineering from the University of Tulsa in Oklahoma.
forbes_facts: His brother, Antonio Ermirio de Moraes, unsuccessfully ran to become governor of Sao Paulo, Brazil's richest state. He died in 2014.

name: Brunello Cucinelli
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: The "king of cashmere," designer Brunello Cucinelli dropped out of engineering school and used a $550 loan to launch a fashion line in 1978.
Inspired by brightly colored wool sweaters, he set out to create a similar garment in cashmere.
Today his eponymous luxury brand is best known for those cashmere sweaters, but also sells dresses, suits, shoes, handbags and accessories.
Cucinelli took the $1.6 billion (2025 revenues) company public in 2012, listing its shares on the Italian stock exchange.
Since 1985 he has operated Brunello Cucinelli SpA from his headquarters in Solomeo, a medieval Italian hamlet that he has renovated for his employees.
forbes_facts: Cucinelli contributed to the reconstruction of several monuments in the central Italian town of Norcia, which was damaged in a 2016 earthquake.
He does not allow work after 5:30 pm and serves 90-minute homemade lunches prepared by the housewives of Solomeo.

name: Ankur Jain
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Ankur Jain founded and runs home rental rewards startup Bilt Rewards, which raised $250 million from private investors at a $10.75 billion valuation in July 2025.
Bilt Rewards processes rent payments and enables renters to earn and redeem points with airlines, hotels, gyms and restaurants.
Jain, who is CEO, owns 32% of Bilt Rewards, which is based in New York City.
Jain previously cofounded Humin, an app that combined contacts, calendars and more and was acquired by Tinder; he made the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in 2015.
Jain's father, former Microsoft executive Naveen Jain, was briefly a billionaire in 2000 when shares of InfoSpace, the Internet content firm he founded, peaked.
forbes_facts: Longtime NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell joined Bilt Rewards' board as an independent director in 2024.
Ken Chenault, former chairman of American Express, became chairman of Bilt Rewards in 2024 after venture capital firm General Catalyst, where Chenault now works, invested in Bilt.

name: Kim Jun-ki
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Kim Jun-ki, founder of the Dongbu Group, stepped down as its chairman in 2017 after being accused of rape and sexual harassment.
In 2020 Kim was convicted of the sexual assault charges and was sentenced to two and a half years in prison, which was suspended for four years.
Dongbu, now named DB, has interests in chemicals, finance, electronics and real estate.
His net worth includes the shares of his only son, Kim Nam-ho, who is honorary chairman as well as his daughter.
He is a son of a former deputy speaker in the South Korean parliament.
forbes_facts: He started the company with two employees and the equivalent of $25,000.
During a 40-day overseas trip in 1969, inspired by what he saw in Japan and the U.S., he withdrew his studies and started a construction company.

name: J. Tomilson Hill
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Mergers and acquisitions maven J. Tomilson "Tom" Hill started off his career at investment bank First Boston, where he cofounded the M&A department.
Hill later became a partner at Lehman Brothers in the 1980s, where he befriended Blackstone cofounders Pete Peterson and Stephen Schwarzman.
In 1993, after being ousted as co-CEO at Lehman, he joined Peterson and Schwarzman at Blackstone, their growing private equity firm.
Hill, who took over Blackstone's hedge fund group in 2000 and became vice chairman in 2007, stepped down from his position in 2019.
He now heads the Hill Art Foundation and is CEO of hedge fund Two Sigma's real estate business and chairman of its private investments business.
forbes_facts: While at Lehman, Hill was involved in high profile deals such as Time Inc.'s $14 billion merger with Warner Communications, which created media behemoth Time Warner.
Hill is an avid art collector, with a collection that reportedly includes pieces by Andy Warhol and Francis Bacon.

name: Jurgen Wirtgen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Jurgen Wirtgen is one of two billionaire brothers who inherited the family fortune from their father, Reinhard, founder of construction equipment maker Wirtgen Group.
Wirtgen group was founded in 1961 and sold to Deere & Company in 2017 for $5.2 billion.
After the sale, the brothers created Wirtgen Invest, a family office with interests in energy, real estate, healthcare, consumer goods and finance.
The investment firm has made some 700 generally passive investments, according to its website.

name: Robert G. Miller
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022-2024); Forbes annual (2000-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Canadian  Robert Miller cofounded electronics distributor Future Electronics in 1968.
He stepped down as CEO in 2023 after an investigation alleged that he paid underage girls for sex. Miller denied the allegations.
In 2024, he sold Future Electronics to Taiwan-based WT Microelectronics in a $3.8 billion deal, likely pocketing ten figures from the sale.
Miller was arrested by Montreal police in May 2024 and charged with 21 sex crimes counts. He vowed to "vigorously protect his reputation, fight for the truth and refute these false allegations."
In June 2025, a Quebec Superior Court judge deemed Miller, who is suffering from Parkinson's disease, too sick to stand trial and ordered a stay of proceedings
forbes_facts: Miller rarely grants interviews or attends public ceremonies, and does not allow his picture to be taken.
Miller believes in cryonics, the science of freezing bodies to restore life later on, and supports the cryonics-focused Alcor Life Extension Foundation.

name: Travis Boersma
sec_insider_companies: Dutch Bros Inc. (BROS) - Executive Chairman of Board
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Travis Boersma is the cofounder and executive chairman of Oregon-based coffee chain Dutch Bros.
Boersma took Dutch Bros public on the New York Stock Exchange in September 2021; he owns nearly 60 million shares.
He and his late brother Dane (d. 2009) started selling coffee from a pushcart in Grants Pass, Oregon in 1992 after quitting the family dairy business.
Dutch Bros, which added the first of its now popular drive-through locations in 1994, now has over 1000 shops in 19 states.
The company is known for its quirky culture; its baristas are called "broistas" and it offers beverages such as the "Hot Annihilator."

name: Sergei Sudarikov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Sergei Sudarikov is the main shareholder of Region Group, which includes banking, pension fund, insurance, brokerage and asset management companies.
Sudarikov began at Region in 1995 as a trader. In 2011, he and a group of partners bought the business from its founder.
Region bought several asset management businesses from state-owned oil firm Rosneft in 2011, helping it become one of Russia's largest investment groups.
In 2019, Sudarikov agreed to merge his assets with billionaire Roman Avdeev's Rossium concern, active in finance, real estate development and oil.
He bought Avdeev's stake and became owner of 93% of Rossium in 2024.
forbes_facts: Sudarikov's main hobby is wild fishing. He caught his first fish at the age of three.
According to Sudarikov, his first business was selling books in the early 1990s.

name: Gavril Yushvaev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Gavril Yushvaev has gotten rich betting on a wide assortment of businesses.
In the early 1990s Yushvaev cofounded Trinity, which owned Moscow dance club Metelitsa, one of the city's first casinos, and car dealerships.
He later invested in dairy and juice company Wimm-Bill-Dann, which went public in 2002.
Yushvaev sold his 19.6% stake in Wimm-Bill-Dann to Pepsico for $1.1 billion in 2010.
He has reportedly invested $500 million in European and U.S. tech start-ups including driver app Lyft and delivery service Delivery Hero.
In 2022 Portugal's Publico newspaper reported that Yushvaev is waiting a Portuguese passport. He certified by the Israeli Community of Porto as a descendant of Sephardic Jews.
forbes_facts: Wimm-Bill-Dann's prospectus for its 2002 IPO revealed that Yushvaev served nine years in a Soviet prison camp after being found guilty of a "violent crime" in 1980.
Yushvaev and Vladislav Doronin, an ex-boyfriend of supermodel Naomi Campbell, invested $300 million in a 4.3-million-square-foot Moscow real estate development.

name: Chi Yufeng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Chi Yufeng chairs Shenzhen-listed online games firm Perfect World.
Chi holds an undergraduate degree in chemistry from prestigious Tsinghua University and a MBA from CEIBS.
He is also known as Michael Chi.

name: Anand Surana
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2016-2019)
forbes_bio: Anand Surana is a director at pharma company Micro Labs known for the popular paracetamol Dolo.
The Bangalore-headquartered generics company makes drugs for cardiac diseases, diabetes and pain management.
The privately held Micro Labs gets nearly 60% of its annual revenue from the domestic market.
It also makes ophthalmic products for Bausch & Lomb's Asia-Pacific market.
India's tax authority alleged in July 2022 that Micro Labs gave freebies worth 10 billion rupees to doctors to push drug sales. The company denied any wrongdoing.
forbes_facts: The company was founded by their late father G.C. Surana, a former pharma distributor, in 1973 in Chennai.
During the pandemic, sales of the company's paracetamol brand Dolo 650 soared.
